doc.title: Hinton Milt — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Cab Calloway's band: road, arrangers and shows
title: Cab Calloway's band personnel in 1936, from the Missourians to Dizzy Gillespie
summary: Hinton lists the trumpets, drummer and trombones in Cab's band when he joined and mentions his itinerary book.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: See that takeover and the band that I joined, Cab Calloway of 1936, the last of „35, was the nucleus, was the Missourians. All those guys were still there. Leroy Maxie who was the drummer, was still there and Foots Thomas was also… was there. Andrew Brown was still there. Depris Wheeler, a trombone player was there, was still in the band then… and I‟m missing Lemar Wright.
Who else was in the trumpet section, do you remember?

Well later Mouse Randolph, Irving Randolph was… trumpet, and Doc Cheetum. he came in there, not too… he came in there. Because Doc stayed… let‟s see it was Lemar Wright, Irving Randolph, and Doc Cheetum. Then we added… there was three trumpets at first when I came in about that time. Then they added a fourth trumpet and I think it was Chet Collins. Then Doc Cheetum got sick and went home to recuperate and someone recommended Dizzy and Dizzy came in and Doc never came back until years later in his „70s or something. We went down to South America.
Were you in the band when Dizzy was in the band?
Oh, yeah, sure. I was in there when he came in the band.
Was Mario in that band, Mario Obosser?

Mario Obosser came in later, yeah, about „39 or something like that. I think… I can‟t remember who… I‟ve got a book downstairs with exactly… with all our itinerary and who left and who was in their place.

Yeah. Some guy followed… Cab Calloway always said, “Well if you want to know anything about me, see Milt because he‟s got all the [laughter]… I even know the numbers of all the music that was in his book. Well you don‟t stay in a band 16 years without…
[Unintelligible] that way about it. It was a career for me. I thought it would last forever.
What was it like when you… prior to going with… what were you doing
I was gigging. I was down at the Three Deuces with Zooty Singleton and [unintelligible]. That‟s where Cab came down and hired me, that night from there.
